newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pioneer seen returning to recovery path in 1st qtr.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer seen returning to recovery path in 1st qtr.

text.p: Japanese audio-visual equipment maker Pioneer Electronic Corp's earnings are expected to have returned to a steady recovery track in the April-June quarter, helped by drastic payroll cuts and a weak yen, analysts said on Friday.
But they were divided on whether profits for the first fiscal quarter for 1997/98 would be strong enough to compel the company to raise its profit forecasts for the year to March 31, 1998.
Pioneer will announce its results for the April-June quarter on August 18.
The company's share price firmed on Friday on speculation of robust earnings growth in the quarter, closing at 2,770 yen on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, up 220 yen from Thursday's close.
Analysts expect Pioneer to announce a group net profit of 1.5 billion to two billion yen in the quarter, up from 804 million yen in the year-ago period.

"A programme to cut personnel in 1996/97 and the weak yen set the company on a recovery track, while smooth sales of DVD (digital video disc) players were a good sign," said Yoshiharu Izumi, an analyst at UBS Securities Co.

"We expect its group net profit to reach 10 billion yen in 1997/98, exceeding the company's estimate of eight billion yen," he said, adding that UBS has set a target price for Pioneer's shares at 3,500 yen.

Under an early-retirement plan, Pioneer reduced its workforce by 998, from an original total of 7,300, in 1996/97 in a bid to bolster its bottom line, which was hit hard by sluggish sales of its mainstay products, mainly laser disc players.
Other analysts were less bullish on Pioneer's first quarter results, citing sluggish sales of audio products in the United States and of car electronics at home.
"I don't think the first quarter results will be that positive (compared with market speculation)," said Masaru Koshida, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"It will be only after July that higher sales of DVD players will start making a contribution to profits," he said.
Fumiya Seko, an analyst at Yamaichi Research Institute, added: "The benefits of the restructuring plans and the weak yen rate have already been discounted in the market.
"It's hard to find strong reasons to buy (Pioneer shares) in the short term, as the big players in the audio-visual field will eventually get the lion's share of the DVD player market," he said.
